request.spec:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The screen now has a header with the counters, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**What's new:** `src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx` puts a header at the top of the sheet, above every other section. It shows:
- **People:** everyone on the sheet, retired people included (`header-people-count`).
- **Claims by status:** one count each for DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED and VOID (`header-claims-<STATUS>-count`).
- **Due total and overdue total** (`header-due-total`, `header-overdue-total`).

**Keeping them equal:** each counter uses the same data and the same arithmetic as the figure it repeats, so they can't drift apart. I moved the list of statuses and the per-status count out of the summary into a new shared file, `features/summary/statusCounts.ts`, which both the summary and the header now use. The summary looks the same as before. The two totals are added up the same way as the existing due and overdue totals.

No server, database or audit changes were needed, because everything the header shows was already loaded on the screen. The header appears once a sheet is loaded, since its counts belong to that sheet.
